tools_helpful.evidence: Bootstrap scaffolded the WinUI3 shell and mass-rewrote Windows.UI.Xaml -> Microsoft.UI.Xaml across copied .cs/.xaml; root-namespace guard ran. Migration proceeded file-by-file from MIGRATION-MAPPING.md.

tool_limitations.limitation: The mass namespace rewrite only handles the Windows.UI.Xaml.* family (script line 113: $orig -replace 'Windows\.UI\.Xaml','Microsoft.UI.Xaml'). Sibling non-Xaml Windows.UI.* namespaces (Windows.UI for Colors/ColorHelper, Windows.UI.Text for FontWeights, Windows.UI.Core dispatcher) are left untouched, so simple-name references like Colors.Red surface as CS0103 later.
tool_limitations.suggested_tweak: Document the remaining non-Xaml Windows.UI.* remap as a build-error remedy (cannot be a blind script rewrite because the Windows.UI namespace splits type-by-type: the Color struct stays Windows.UI.Color while Colors/ColorHelper move to Microsoft.UI).

failed_apis.why_tried: AdaptiveStreaming Scenario3 modifies network requests using the WinRT Windows.Web.Http stack (IHttpFilter / HttpBaseProtocolFilter).
failed_apis.root_cause: WinUI3 desktop projects reference the .NET BCL System.Net.Http by default; the UWP source uses Windows.Web.Http. Both namespaces define HttpMethod, HttpClient, HttpResponseMessage, HttpRequestMessage and HttpCompletionOption, so unqualified use becomes CS0104 ambiguous.
failed_apis.fix: Keep the Windows.Web.Http stack (its IHttpFilter surface has no System.Net.Http equivalent) and resolve the collision by removing/aliasing the conflicting System.Net.Http using or fully-qualifying the WinRT types.

special_apis.special_handling: Colors static class moves to Microsoft.UI.Colors, but the Color struct itself stays Windows.UI.Color — a per-type split, so it cannot be a whole-namespace using rewrite.

errors_encountered.error: LogView.xaml.cs(112): CS0103 'Colors' does not exist in the current context
errors_encountered.root_cause: Code used the unqualified Colors static class; the bootstrap rewrite only touches Windows.UI.Xaml.*, so the file lost no Xaml using but never gained 'using Microsoft.UI;' for the Colors class.

errors_encountered.error: Scenario3_RequestModification.xaml.cs(323/326): CS0104 'HttpMethod' / 'HttpCompletionOption' is an ambiguous reference (System.Net.Http vs Windows.Web.Http)
errors_encountered.root_cause: Both the BCL and WinRT HTTP stacks are in scope; the UWP sample uses Windows.Web.Http.
errors_encountered.fix: Remove or alias the System.Net.Http using and keep the Windows.Web.Http types, or fully qualify them.

errors_encountered.root_cause: Dispatcher.RunAsync(CoreDispatcherPriority.Normal, ...) was left un-migrated in Scenario5 even though MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md#threading prescribes DispatcherQueue.TryEnqueue. Most other files were migrated; Scenario5 was missed before the budget ran out.

errors_encountered.error: Scenario5_Metadata.xaml.cs(560): CS0165 use of unassigned local 'currentPosition'
errors_encountered.root_cause: Ordinary uninitialized-local coding mistake introduced during edit; unrelated to any UWP API.

Downstream cascade: the XAML pre-compile (_OnXamlPreCompileError) crashes when the partial-class code-behind does not compile (the CS0103/CS0104 errors above). Distinct from the namespace-collision WMC9999 that the bootstrap root-namespace guard already prevents.
errors_encountered.fix: Resolve the C# compile errors first; the WMC9999 clears once code-behind compiles.

dev_agent_struggles.turns_or_retries: final build (_OnXamlPreCompileError) still running after 600s when the log ends
dev_agent_struggles.root_cause: A partial migration was declared/timed-out with build errors outstanding; threading/Colors/Http adaptations were applied to most files but missed in Scenario5/LogView/Scenario3.
dev_agent_struggles.how_resolved: not resolved — ran out of budget
dev_agent_struggles.preventable_by: Faster inline resolution of the common build-error families (CS0104 Http ambiguity, CS0103 non-Xaml Windows.UI simple names) via a 'Common build errors' entry the agent hits directly, so each error is a one-line lookup-and-fix instead of an open-ended investigation.
